To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
COX- 2 immunoreactivity is upregulated in human brain in the first few days following cerebral ischemic infraction.

COX- 2 immunoreactivity is observed in infiltrating polymorphonuclear leukocytes, in vascular cells, and in neurons located in the border zone of the infarcts in human brains that died 1–3 days after the ischemic insult.
COX- 2 is up-regulated during cerebral ischemic injury in the human brain, and this is likely to contribute to the pathophysiological processes leading to ischemic injury.
